query: Earlier empirical-potential and first-principles studies primarily targeted phase-transition temperature, while other fusion properties remain difficult because they require free energies on both sides of the transition with vibrational entropy, anharmonicity, and electron–vibration coupling retained. Explicit ab initio free-energy evaluation is highly accurate but depends on costly molecular dynamics. TOR-TILD increased throughput for elemental and binary systems, yet slows substantially for multicomponent high-entropy systems. Under the constraint that the free energies of both solid and fluid states and the relevant entropy terms remain faithful, what single testable methodological hypothesis could substantially reduce the cost of obtaining fusion and high-temperature thermodynamic properties? State the proposed intervention and why it should work, predict its speed and fidelity relative to explicit ab initio molecular-dynamics workflows and TOR-TILD, define composition and temperature boundaries, cite supporting evidence from prior elemental or binary results, and specify a decisive benchmark of phase free energies and derived observables that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: For multicomponent concentrated alloys, free energies of both crystalline and liquid phases that include vibrational, anharmonic and electron–phonon contributions can be obtained at two to three orders-of-magnitude lower wall-clock cost than explicit ab-initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) or TOR-TILD by coupling (i) an on-the-fly actively learned equivariant-graph neural-network potential (GNNP) with (ii) a single-stage thermodynamic‐integration (TI) correction that perturbs the GNNP Hamiltonian to the DFT Hamiltonian on < O(10²) statistically independent snapshots from each phase.
generation.material_initial_state: Face-centred-cubic equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi high-entropy alloy (solid phase) and its corresponding equilibrium melt at 0–30 GPa, 300–2500 K.
generation.intervention: Train a symmetric equivariant GNNP during short seeding AIMD runs covering solid and liquid; use the converged GNNP to run long (>2 ns) NPT molecular-dynamics trajectories (10³–10⁴ atoms). Obtain (a) solid free energy via the Frenkel–Ladd Einstein–crystal route and (b) liquid free energy via reversible solid–liquid TI. Apply a final free-energy correction ΔF = −kBT ln⟨exp[−(UDFT − UGNNP)/kBT]⟩GNNP computed on 50–100 decorrelated configurations per phase.
generation.conditions: Pressures 0–30 GPa; temperatures 300–2500 K; compositions restricted to quinary FCC Co–Cr–Fe–Mn–Ni with equiatomic or near-equiatomic (±10 at.% each element) chemistry.
generation.structural_mediator: Actively learned equivariant graph neural-network interatomic potential that reproduces the DFT potential-energy surface for both solid and liquid local environments.
generation.mechanism: The GNNP supplies DFT-level forces at ~10⁵× lower cost, enabling statistically converged thermodynamic integration paths with large supercells. The final ΔF perturbative step systematically removes residual GNNP bias, so vibrational, anharmonic and electron–phonon entropy terms remain faithful to DFT.
generation.predicted_outcome: Fusion enthalpy, fusion entropy, and melting temperature will match fully explicit AIMD within ±5 meV atom⁻¹, ±0.05 kB atom⁻¹, and ±50 K, respectively, while requiring ≤1% of the CPU time of AIMD and ~10% of TOR-TILD time for the same alloy.
generation.baseline: 1. Explicit two-phase coexistence or reversible‐scaling AIMD free-energy calculations (current gold standard). 2. TOR-TILD as reported for binary systems (best current reduced-cost alternative).
generation.boundary: Fails when (a) chemistries stray >10 at.% from the active-learning training manifold, (b) temperatures exceed ~0.8 T_electronic-exc where strong electronic excitations dominate (>3000 K for 3d HEAs), or (c) structural motifs (e.g., B2 clusters) absent from the training data appear.
generation.uncertainty: Risk that short AIMD seed may miss rare liquid configurations, leading to GNNP extrapolation; electron–vibration coupling corrections may not be fully captured by the perturbative ΔF if local DOS changes sharply with configuration.

falsification_experiment.design: Compute solid and liquid free energies of equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi at 1800 K and 0 GPa using the proposed GNNP+TI method and, independently, fully converged 10 ps AIMD thermodynamic integration with 150-atom supercells.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If |F_solid − F_liquid|, ΔF_fusion, or predicted T_m differ from the AIMD reference by >10 meV atom⁻¹, >15 meV atom⁻¹, or >50 K, respectively, the hypothesis is falsified.
